results.title: Hintly - AI Meeting Assistant for Google Meet™ - Chrome Web Store
results.content: Hintly is a live AI explainer for Google Meet. When someone mentions a term, acronym, name or reference you don't know, Hintly shows a short explanation beside the call a moment later, so you can keep following the conversation instead of nodding along. What Hintly does - Explains jargon, acronyms and terms as they're said "We're seeing split-brain after the failover." A card appears: Split-brain, two databases both acting as primary. Hover it for one more line of context. - Fills in the blanks When someone can't remember a name ("that book about the desert planet with the giant worms"), Hintly works out what they mean and names it for you: Dune. - Live fact checking When someone states something that's clearly false, like the wrong year or the wrong inventor, Hintly quietly shows the [...] wrong year or the wrong inventor, Hintly quietly shows the right answer. It's strict: only plainly wrong facts are flagged, never opinions, estimates, plans or recent news. - Keeps track of who's who People, projects and clients mentioned earlier in the call come back as a reminder when they're mentioned again. "Priya: moving to the Berlin office in March." - Stays out of your way Hintly stays quiet until something is worth explaining. Cards sit near the top of the call, clear themselves after a few seconds and never cover the people you're talking to. Click a card to dismiss it. - Comes with you between tabs Switch to your notes or inbox and your hints follow you in Meet's floating picture-in-picture window. How it works 1. Install Hintly and sign in with Google. 2. Join a Google Meet [...] securely to Hintly's server to write each hint and is not stored. Hintly never records audio or video and never keeps a transcript of your calls. Memories of people and projects last only for the current call. results.title: Google Meet Is Working Again, and Users Say, Really, You Didn't Need to Rush - CNET
results.content:
“The issue with Google Meet began at 10:25 PDT on 2025-09-08 and has been resolved for all affected users as of 2025-09-08 11:18 PDT,” Google says in an update. “From preliminary analysis, the root cause of the issue is a recent change in content edge cache. Our engineers have resolved the issue by rolling back the change. We thank you for your patience while we worked on resolving the issue.”

### Not everyone is sad about Google Meet's issues

Since Google Meet is often used for work meetings and school classes or conferences, not everyone was sad to see the program go down.

Several users posted celebratory GIFs — scenes from The Office were favorites.

Another wrote, “Attention: Google Meet is down. Time to catch up on emails or go touch grass.”
